analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/developer/test.md (head text units 6 and 7, lines 475-1362) and docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md (patch plus base text). No executable code or threat-model YAML changed in the supplied units. The describes-behavior changes concern TB-012, A-018 and T-059, the add-on hold socket. They document: (1) addon-hold.json opened with O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW and accepted only as an owner-only regular file of at most 64 KiB, so a FIFO is ignored. That limits a same-UID local DoS via a blocking read. (2) A 10 s per-line requestTimeout that closes slow-drip connections. (3) Peer verification at accept time, before a connection takes one of the 8 slots, with re-verification on every request. This reduces slot-exhaustion by unverified or silent peers. (4) A clarification that DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET is honored in every build but not passed by the LaunchAgent. This doc line is a possible environment-override surface. I cannot confirm from these units whether release builds honor it in a way a same-UID process could abuse. The socket is already same-UID and peer-verified, so I treat it as a consistency note, not a regression. The docs now cite a new threat ID T-060 and a new local-control.md page. Neither definition is in the supplied index. The next pass should confirm that T-060 and docs/architecture/security/local-control.md exist in the threat model at the head revision. The test.md edits add test filters (AddonHoldLoadFence, FIFO mailbox, Super slot retirement). They also state the peer check is exercised only negatively and that physical add-on interoperation remains separate, which is honest scoping. I could not verify that the documented controls match the Swift sources (AddonIPCServer, AddonHoldStore), because those files were not supplied. No concrete security regression is identified in the documentation.
